column2: Since the sickness came to [capital.GetName] the streets have filled with cats. They pick through the rubbish behind the empty houses and yowl all night on the rooftops, and the people are sure they carry the pestilence from door to door.
Gather some cats to be examined.
You pay the rat-catchers to bring cats in instead of rats.\n
The cats are not to blame.

[cat_examiner.GetFirstName] reports that, apart from making their displeasure at being caught very plain, most of the cats seem calm and healthy. Only a few show any sign of sickness. It is unlikely the cats are the cause.
So the cats are innocent. Let them go.
Keep a few to watch.
The complaints about the cats will not stop. A mob has gathered outside the gates, shouting that cats are the familiars of witches and cannot be let to roam the streets.
Kill the 'source'.
You pick the meanest-looking cat from the sample and have it hanged in the square.
Cats are not the cause.
You calm the mob with a rousing speech.
The cats are mostly healthy.
You do your best to explain what the examination found.
Get rid of all the cats!
This is absurd. Go home.

[worried_courtier.GetFirstName] has heard that I mean to be rid of every cat in the city. 'Healthy cats should not be harmed for the people's fear. I cannot accept it!' [worried_courtier.GetSheHe] says.
I am sorry, [worried_courtier.GetFirstName]. Your cats too.
We can keep it secret. But you owe me.

[worried_courtier.GetFirstName] should have hidden [worried_courtier.GetHerHis] cats better. They have been seen, and now the people are furious that their [Root.GetTitle] kept a nest of witches' beasts at court.
Curse you, [worried_courtier.GetFirstName]!
One of the cats taken for examination has grown fond of you. It gives a sweet mew whenever you pass its cage and purrs when you come close.
I will call her 'Whiskers'.
I will call her 'Mittens'.
I will call her 'Boots'.
The people would not approve.
[From.GetTitledName] has ordered every cat in the realm killed. You have grown fond of the cats about your court, and the thought of it is horribly upsetting.
I will ask for an exception.
[From.GetTitledName] will hear your plea.
I cannot argue with my liege.
[From.GetTitledName] has refused to make an exception.
That [GetRootFromInsult]!
[From.GetTitledName] has agreed to let me keep my cats, in return for a favour.
What a relief.
After months of talk about cats, the common folk seem to have found other things to worry about.
Good.
Unhappy with how I handled the matter, the peasants now demand not only that every cat be killed, but that their taxes be lowered to make up for my neglect.
A fair demand.
You have no power here!

The peasants of my realm have become convinced that the Strigany wanderers brought the sickness. Their painted wagons were seen on the roads before the first death, and everyone knows the Strigany keep company with witches and worse. Some press me to condemn them, others to protect them.
Something must be done!
...but I do not really care.

There is unrest in the [From.PrimaryTitle.GetFullName]. The peasants say the Strigany caused the sickness there, and if nothing is done they may take matters into their own hands and start killing them.
Only a follower of [Root.Religion.GetRandomEvilGodNameCap] could believe that!
The Strigany did cause it. [Root.Religion.GetHighGodNameCap] has shown me!
[Root.RelHead.GetTitledFirstName] has made it clear that the Strigany are not to be blamed for the sickness, but not everyone is listening. I must still decide what to do.
[Root.RelHead.GetTitledFirstName] has joined in condemning the Strigany, but I am still not sure it is right. I am [Root.GetTitle] here, after all.
Everyone seems to be condemning the Strigany, but I am still not sure they brought the sickness. As [Root.GetTitle], the decision is mine.
No. The Strigany are not to blame.
The Strigany did this. Drive them out!
The Strigany caravans in the realm are broken up and every Strigany courtier is banished.
Word has reached me that a mob means to purge the Strigany camp outside [pogrom_city_target.GetName], despite my decree that they are not to blame for the sickness.
Word has reached me that a mob means to purge the Strigany camped by a nearby village, despite my decree that they are not to blame for the sickness.
Send soldiers to stop them.
Let them do it.

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName] from [From.GetTitledFirstName].\n\nI have heard of the trouble in [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetFullName]. I must ask that you keep the Strigany safe. Wanderers they may be, but they did not bring this sickness, and the gods will not look kindly on murder done in their name.

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName] from [From.GetTitledFirstName].\n\nI have heard of the trouble in [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetFullName], and I agree with your people. The Strigany are thieves and friends of the restless dead, and this sickness is their doing. Drive them out or kill them, I care not which.

Witch Hunter [From.GetFirstName] has come to you with grim news. The sickness emptying your realm is no natural thing, [From.GetSheHe] says: it is the work of servants of the Dark Gods hiding among your own people. [From.GetSheHeCap] asks for your leave to root them out.

Your [Root.GetLordSpiritualName] [From.GetFirstName] has brought you troubling news. Word is spreading that worshippers of [Root.Religion.GetRandomEvilGodName] are behind the terrible sickness ravaging your realm. [From.GetTitledFirstName] urges you to look into it.
Horrifying news! Find them, [From.GetFirstName].

You set [From.GetFirstName] to hunt for witches and sorcerers.

All of your demesne gets §Y'Peasant Unrest'§! until the hunt ends, giving the following effects:
Local Revolt Risk: §R+10.0%§!
Local Tax Modifier: §R-50.0%§!
Nonsense! There are no witches here!

You dismiss the rumours and [From.GetFirstName]'s concerns.

All of your demesne gets §Y'Peasant Crisis'§! for 10 years, giving the following effects:
Local Revolt Risk: §R+15.0%§!
Local Tax Modifier: §R-75.0%§!

[bg_witch_hunter.GetTitledFirstName] has brought you a worrying number of people who swear they have seen witchcraft done: lights in empty windows, beasts born with too many eyes, chanting in the cellars at night. If they are to be believed, the servants of [Root.Religion.GetRandomEvilGodName] are many and a great danger to your realm.
[bg_witch_hunter.GetFirstName], find these heretics before it is too late!
You send [bg_witch_hunter.GetFirstName] to find any witches and sorcerers at your court.\n
Warn the court. Everyone must be watchful!
You make sure all your courtiers watch for signs of witchcraft.\n
Actually, I already have my suspicions...
You take the chance to denounce someone you dislike as a witch.\n
These stories are ridiculous. Stop wasting my time!
You dismiss the witnesses and [bg_witch_hunter.GetFirstName]'s concerns.\n

[From.GetTitledFirstName] lays a bundle on the table before you: a knife of black iron, a book bound in skin, and a brass amulet worked with a symbol that hurts the eye. All of it was found hidden in the chambers of [bg_likely_witch.GetTitledFirstName]. There is no doubt this time. [bg_likely_witch.GetSheHeCap] serves the Dark Gods.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] is certain that [bg_likely_witch.GetTitledFirstName] is the [bg_likely_witch.GetWarlockWitch] at your court. [bg_likely_witch.GetSheHeCap] bears the touch of the Warp, plain for anyone who cares to look, and such things do not happen to the pure of heart.

After a thorough investigation, [From.GetTitledFirstName] has decided that [bg_likely_witch.GetTitledFirstName] is most likely the [bg_likely_witch.GetWarlockWitch] at your court. [bg_likely_witch.GetSheHeCap] has been heard talking to [bg_likely_witch.GetHerselfHimself] in strange tongues, and a few poor souls have even been attacked by [bg_likely_witch.GetHerHim].

After a thorough investigation, [From.GetTitledFirstName] has decided that [bg_likely_witch.GetTitledFirstName] is most likely the [bg_likely_witch.GetWarlockWitch] at your court. Everyone knows [bg_likely_witch.GetFirstName] to be a most sinful [bg_likely_witch.GetManWoman], and one so steeped in vice must be consorting with [Root.Religion.GetRandomEvilGodName].

After a thorough investigation, [From.GetTitledFirstName] has decided that [bg_likely_witch.GetTitledFirstName] is most likely the [bg_likely_witch.GetWarlockWitch] at your court. [From.GetFirstName] says [From.GetSheHe] found forbidden writings in [bg_likely_witch.GetFirstName]'s chambers, proof that [bg_likely_witch.GetSheHe] is no true servant of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName].

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has brought you distressing news: [From.GetSheHe] is certain that [bg_likely_witch.GetTitledFirstName] is a [bg_likely_witch.GetWarlockWitch]! [From.GetSheHeCap] has heard [bg_likely_witch.GetFirstName] talking to [bg_likely_witch.GetHerselfHimself] in a strange tongue, and tells you of several times [bg_likely_witch.GetSheHe] has attacked others at court.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] comes to you with a most serious accusation: [From.GetSheHe] believes [bg_likely_witch.GetTitledFirstName] is a [bg_likely_witch.GetWarlockWitch]! Everyone knows [bg_likely_witch.GetFirstName] to be a most sinful [bg_likely_witch.GetManWoman], [From.GetSheHe] says, and one so steeped in vice must be consorting with [Root.Religion.GetRandomEvilGodName].

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has told you something unsettling. [From.GetSheHeCap] has reason to believe [bg_likely_witch.GetTitledFirstName] is a [bg_likely_witch.GetWarlockWitch]! [From.GetSheHeCap] found forbidden writings in [bg_likely_witch.GetFirstName]'s chambers, proof that [bg_likely_witch.GetSheHe] is no true servant of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName].
You must be right, [From.GetFirstName]! Take [bg_likely_witch.GetHerHim] to the cells!

§Y[bg_likely_witch.GetTitledFirstName]§! will be imprisoned until the day of judgement.

All of your demesne gets §Y'Peasants Pleased With Witch Hunt'§! for 60 days, giving the following effects:
Local Revolt Risk: §G-10.0%§!
Preposterous! [bg_likely_witch.GetFirstName] is a faithful servant of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName]!
You dismiss what §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! told you.\n

[bg_rival_1.GetTitledFirstName] and [bg_rival_2.GetTitledFirstName] burst into your hall, shouting over each other. Each swears the other is a witch. The charges are dire, but there is no proof either way. You have only your gut to go on.
[bg_rival_1.GetTitledFirstName] must be a [bg_rival_1.GetWarlockWitch]!

§Y[bg_rival_1.GetTitledFirstName]§! will be imprisoned until the day of judgement.

All of your demesne gets §Y'Peasants Pleased With Witch Hunt'§! for 60 days, giving the following effects:
Local Revolt Risk: §G-10.0%§!
The only [bg_rival_2.GetWarlockWitch] here is [bg_rival_2.GetTitledFirstName]!

§Y[bg_rival_2.GetTitledFirstName]§! will be imprisoned until the day of judgement.

All of your demesne gets §Y'Peasants Pleased With Witch Hunt'§! for 60 days, giving the following effects:
Local Revolt Risk: §G-10.0%§!
I am no fool! You both worship [Root.Religion.GetRandomEvilGodName]!

§Y[bg_rival_1.GetTitledFirstName]§! and §Y[bg_rival_2.GetTitledFirstName]§! will be imprisoned until the day of judgement.

All of your demesne gets §Y'Peasants Pleased With Witch Hunt'§! for 60 days, giving the following effects:
Local Revolt Risk: §G-10.0%§!
This is absurd! Get out of my sight!
You send §Y[bg_rival_1.GetTitledFirstName]§! and §Y[bg_rival_2.GetTitledFirstName]§! away.\n

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has told you damning things about [bg_spouse.GetTitledFirstName]. [From.GetSheHeCap] says [bg_spouse.GetSheHe] consorts with [Root.Religion.GetRandomEvilGodName] and must be stopped for everyone's good, above all for the sake of [bg_spouse.GetHerHis] poor [bg_lover.GetHusbandWife], [bg_lover.GetTitledFirstName].
I will protect [bg_lover.GetHerHim] from this wicked [bg_spouse.GetWarlockWitch]!

§Y[bg_spouse.GetTitledFirstName]§! will be imprisoned until the day of judgement.

All of your demesne gets §Y'Peasants Pleased With Witch Hunt'§! for 60 days, giving the following effects:
Local Revolt Risk: §G-10.0%§!
Keep your nose out of other people's marriages!
You dismiss what §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! told you.\n
You have taken some time to think. Whom at court could you name a witch and get away with it? Now you have a few good names in mind. No one would dare question you...
[bg_dislike_1.GetTitledFirstName] is a [bg_dislike_1.GetWarlockWitch]!

§Y[bg_dislike_1.GetTitledFirstName]§! will be imprisoned until the day of judgement.

All of your demesne gets §Y'Peasants Pleased With Witch Hunt'§! for 60 days, giving the following effects:
Local Revolt Risk: §G-10.0%§!
Seize the heretic [bg_dislike_2.GetTitledFirstName]!

§Y[bg_dislike_2.GetTitledFirstName]§! will be imprisoned until the day of judgement.

All of your demesne gets §Y'Peasants Pleased With Witch Hunt'§! for 60 days, giving the following effects:
Local Revolt Risk: §G-10.0%§!
[bg_dislike_3.GetTitledFirstName] brought this sickness on us!

§Y[bg_dislike_3.GetTitledFirstName]§! will be imprisoned until the day of judgement.

All of your demesne gets §Y'Peasants Pleased With Witch Hunt'§! for 60 days, giving the following effects:
Local Revolt Risk: §G-10.0%§!
I will be merciful and accuse no one.

The day of judgement has come. The pyres are stacked in the square and the crowd has been waiting since dawn. It is time to deal with those who consorted with [Root.Religion.GetRandomEvilGodName] and brought the sickness on your realm. What will you do?
Light the pyres!
§Y'Peasant Unrest'§! will be removed from all of your demesne.\n\n
At least one of the condemned truly served the Dark Gods. The faithful will remember who lit the pyre.
Let them rot in the dungeon.
You leave the prisoners to rot in the dungeon.
Teach them the mercy of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName].

The precautions you took seem to have worked. There has been little talk of witchcraft these last weeks and no new accusations. You will never know for certain if those you condemned brought the sickness, but at least everyone else seems relieved...
I did what I had to do.

It has been many months since the peasants and courtiers began calling for a witch hunt. For all their pointing of fingers, you have found no one you believe truly serves [Root.Religion.GetRandomEvilGodName]. They have given up hope that you will ever find the guilty.
I pray it is over now.

Today you found [From.GetFirstName] stabbed to death in [From.GetHerHis] chamber. You saw the courtiers whisper when [From.GetSheHe] passed them in the corridors, and you did nothing. Now the hatred and fear you helped stir up has taken [From.GetHerHim] from you.

Today you found [From.GetFirstName] stabbed to death in [From.GetHerHis] chamber. You saw the courtiers whisper when [From.GetSheHe] passed them in the corridors, and you did nothing. You could not find the witch, so someone found one for you, and [From.GetFirstName] paid the price.
My [From.GetFirstName]...
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has been killed by people who believed [From.GetHerHim] a [From.GetWarlockWitch].\n

My court [Root.Religion.GetPriestTitle] tells me there is unrest in the realm. The people fear the sickness is the wrath of the gods, and some are saying it is my fault, for I am never seen at the temple.
They are right. I should make more of an effort.
You begin attending the temple twice a day.\n
I cannot risk catching the sickness. Send a double!
You order your [Root.GetSpymasterName] §Y[blame_spymaster.GetFirstName]§! to hire an actor to go to the temple in your place twice a day.\n
I shall raise a temple for the restless souls.
You order a temple built near [Root.Capital.GetName].\n
I am [Root.GetTitle]! I do as I please.
You let the unrest go on.

I kneel before the altar of the Heldenhammer while the priests read from the Book of Sigmar, and I lay my hand on the cold iron of the hammer carved there. My subjects have seen me at worship every day, but more than that, I feel close again to the God-King who forged the Empire.

I stand bareheaded before the eternal flame of Ulric, as the priests of the White Wolf demand, and I let its cold fire burn on my brow. My subjects have seen me at worship every day, but more than that, I feel close again to the Lord of Winter.
I walk barefoot into the grove of Taal and lay a stag's antler on the moss-grown stone. My subjects have seen me at worship every day, but more than that, I feel close again to the Lord of the Wild.

I sit in silence in the Garden of Morr among the black-robed priests, and leave a raven feather on a pauper's grave. My subjects have seen me at worship every day, but more than that, I feel close again to the Lord of the Dead, who takes the sick from their pain.

I wash the feet of the sick in the hospice of Shallya and pray with the white-robed sisters for those who will not live through the night. My subjects have seen me at worship every day, but more than that, I feel close again to the Goddess of Mercy.

I sit in the library of Verena's temple while the priests read the old laws aloud, and I leave an owl's quill on the altar. My subjects have seen me at worship every day, but more than that, I feel close again to the Goddess of Wisdom and Justice.

I keep the vigil of Myrmidia with spear and shield before her altar, as her knights do before battle. My subjects have seen me at worship every day, but more than that, I feel close again to the Lady of Battle.
I go down to the harbour shrine of Manann and pour a cup of wine into the grey water. My subjects have seen me at worship every day, but more than that, I feel close again to the Lord of the Seas.

I slip into the little shrine of Ranald behind the tavern and leave a coin and a pair of crossed fingers on the altar. My subjects have seen me at worship every day, but more than that, I feel close again to the Trickster, who loves a ruler that laughs at fate.
I make the offerings at the temple and recite the prayers of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName]. My subjects have seen me at worship every day, but more than that, I feel close to the gods again.
I pray the gods are pleased as well.

My double's daily visits to the temple have calmed the common folk. I sometimes wonder what [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] thinks of me for deceiving my people, but my council agrees: it would do no one any good if the [Root.GetTitle] fell sick.
Let the play go on! Peasants really are too easy to fool.
Depending on your skill at deception, the common folk may or may not be fully calmed.\n\n
I should stop this while I can.
You call off the deception.\n\n

In the misery tormenting our lands, the people of [Root.Capital.GetName] have found new faith in me, their pious [Root.GetTitle]. One family has even offered me their only child as a servant, if I would have them. In their eyes, the child would be serving [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName].
Humble birth or not, the child could make a good servant.
A child named §Y[zealous_child.GetBestName]§! comes to your court.\n§Y'Civil Unrest'§! will be removed from all of your demesne.\n
I do not worship for fame, and I will not tear a child from their family.
You give the family a small gift and suggest they send the child to the temple school instead.\n§Y'Civil Unrest'§! will be removed from all of your demesne.\n
The common folk have found out my ruse! They beat my double to death on the temple steps and set fire to the temple. Now they believe that I, and the gods with me, have abandoned them.
Filthy peasants! How dare they?

All of your demesne gets §Y'Furious Peasants'§! for ten years, giving the following effects:
Local Revolt Risk: §R+25.0%§!
Local Tax Modifier: §R-75.0%§!
I will have to be rid of that worthless [Root.GetSpymasterName] of mine!
You blame it all on your [Root.GetSpymasterName]!\n\n
The actors I hired do not really look like me, but most of the peasants have never seen my face. No wonder they took that ugly impostor for their [Root.GetTitle].
I do love a good ruse.
§Y'Civil Unrest'§! will be removed from all of your demesne.\n
I could not have done it without my trusted [Root.GetSpymasterName].

My speech about the gods demanding everyone's labour put the fear into the common folk. They work day and night, the sickness driving them on in a race against time. But someone has been sabotaging the building, and the culprits have been dragged before me: two starving children from the gutters.
Vandalising a TEMPLE? Off with their heads!

You execute the street urchins, and your workers take heart.

§Y'Civil Unrest'§! will be removed from all of your demesne.
They wanted shelter? They can have it, in prison!
You imprison the vandals.\n\n
These are the villains? They are children!

You take pity on the young vagrants. Two children named §Y[vagrant_child_1.GetBestName]§! and §Y[vagrant_child_2.GetBestName]§! join your court.

All of your demesne gets §Y'Furious Peasants'§! for ten years, giving the following effects:
Local Revolt Risk: §R+25.0%§!
Local Tax Modifier: §R-75.0%§!
The temple is finished, and the people wipe the sweat from their brows. [Root.Religion.GetRandomEvilGodNameCap] cannot take this offering from me. The gods are surely pleased.

Building was already under way on the site I chose for my temple! The builders saw easy money in my orders and 'forgot' to tell me. My [Root.GetTreasurerName] has sorted it out, and at least I get some of my gold back.
Some people do work well under pressure.
§Y'Furious Peasants'§! will be removed from all of your counties.\n
This is most unfortunate!
Your attempt to calm the peasants fails.

[vagrant_child_1.GetBestName] was caught climbing the scaffolding of the new temple at night. [vagrant_child_1.GetHerHisCap] sibling says [vagrant_child_1.GetSheHe] only wanted to see the stars, but a beam gave way and [vagrant_child_1.GetBestName] fell. The workers have put down their tools and say the building is cursed!

In the night the half-built walls of the temple came down, crushing the workers who slept beneath them. The survivors will not go back. They say the building is cursed, and some swear they heard laughter in the rubble!
That foolish child! I never should have taken [vagrant_child_1.GetHerHim] in.

Your attempts to calm the peasants fail.
All of your demesne gets §Y'Furious Peasants'§! for ten years, giving the following effects:
Local Revolt Risk: §R+25.0%§!
Local Tax Modifier: §R-75.0%§!
Superstitious peasants! What about my gold?
A band of flagellant zealots who watched the pyre burn swears itself to your cause (§Y150§! light infantry at half upkeep).
The Dancing Plague

Something very strange is happening in [dancing_plague_outbreak_location.GetName]. It began with one woman dancing alone in the market square. By nightfall there were dozens, and now there are hundreds: men, women and children, whirling through the streets while fiddlers play themselves bloody-fingered. No one sleeps, no one eats, and still they dance. Some have already dropped dead where they stood.\n\nThe priests say it is a curse, the physicians a fever of the blood, and the old women cross themselves and mutter about the Dark Prince. Whatever it is, bands of dancers are already capering down the roads towards the next town.
What madness is this?
After a hearty meal you look out of the window at the dancing crowd below. The music is maddeningly inviting, and you have felt restless of late...

After a hearty meal you look out of the window at the dancing crowd below. The music is maddeningly sweet, and beneath it you hear another tune, one only you seem to hear: a laughing, perfumed voice that promises you have never truly danced. The Prince of Excess is in the streets tonight.
Perhaps I should join their joyous capering!
No. I should rest instead.
I will dance for the Dark Prince!
You give yourself to the dance for Slaanesh. The Prince of Pleasure will be pleased, whatever it costs your feet.\n

Just as you are about to leave, your court physician catches your arm. [target_physician.GetFirstName] warns you not to join the dance, lest you collapse from exhaustion like the rest of them, and begs you to rest instead.
Oh, very well, if you say so.
No! I must dance!

You spend hours dancing with the common folk, and they are amazed! They never thought to see their [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetRulerTitle] caper in the gutter beside them. It is a night they will talk of for years.

You dance with the common folk until dawn, wilder and finer than any of them, and every eye in the square is on you. They never thought to see their [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetRulerTitle] dance like that. Somewhere behind the music you hear the Dark Prince laugh with delight.
I have never had so much fun!

Dancing with the crowd was pleasant at first, but it has quickly grown tiring. Still you have no wish to stop, and when your servants beg you to come home for supper you ignore them. You simply MUST dance!

You lie down to rest but cannot sleep. All you can think of is the music and the dancing... how good it would be to join them in the streets! At last you can bear it no longer and bolt outside to join the revellers.
You dance as if the music were poured into your veins. Your feet bleed and you do not care, because every step is sweeter than the last. The Dark Prince is watching, and he wants more.
I will dance forever!

Months have passed since you first joined the dance. The dancers around you have dropped like flies, from exhaustion, hunger or broken bones. Then, all at once, your feet stop moving and your arms stop flailing.
At last, [Root.Religion.GetRandomEvilGodName] no longer rules my arms and legs!
It never stops! At first you could still rest to eat and sleep, but no longer. Your legs will not let you rest, your hands will not hold food and your mind can hold nothing but the music.
Do not stop me now, I am having such a good time!
After days of dancing without pause, the pain in your legs has become unbearable. Then something snaps! You fall to the ground, unable to take another step. Your dancing days are over.
Aaargh!
A Horrible Affliction

Our people in [plague_outbreak_location.GetName] are dying of a frightening sickness. The stricken break out in great black buboes that creep across the skin like living things, then burn with fever until they vomit blood and die, some in the middle of the street, healthy only days before. Our physicians are helpless and the priests can only pray. Bodies are piling up in the lanes... the Great Plague is at our door.

Our people in [plague_outbreak_location.GetName] are dying of a frightening sickness. Their flesh swells and splits and weeps green pus, and they laugh as they rot, as if someone were whispering a joke only they can hear. Some say flies hatch from the dead within hours. Our physicians are helpless and the priests can only pray. This is no natural sickness: it is Nurgle's Rot, the gift of the Plague God, and it is at our door.
May [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] help us.
Grandfather Nurgle is generous to his children.
The Plague Monks have done well-well. Let the man-things rot!
Word of a Plague

News has come of a great sickness in [plague_outbreak_location.Realm.GetName]. The reports are vague, but people are said to be dying like flies, and the fear of it spreads as fast as the plague itself. No cure is known and no one survives it. With no cause revealed, people are turning to their gods, and on each other, to keep it away. Many call it a Great Plague.
All those poor people.
We must prepare.
May [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] make the heretics suffer.
If I have the chance to help, I will.
Plague only takes the weak.
I knew this would happen!

News has come of a horrible sickness in [plague_outbreak_location.GetName], in [plague_outbreak_location.Realm.GetName]. At first the tales were thought exaggerated, but since ragged refugees began arriving at our gates it is hard to ignore. Our riders tell of black buboes that creep across the skin, of people vomiting blood before they die, of limbs turning black and rotting away. There is no talk of a cure. Only of the death pits.

News has come of a horrible sickness in [plague_outbreak_location.GetName], in [plague_outbreak_location.Realm.GetName]. Since ragged refugees began arriving at our gates it is hard to ignore. They speak of flesh that swells and splits, of the sick laughing as they rot, of the dead rising in clouds of flies, and of rot-cultists dancing in the plague pits. There is no talk of a cure.
[plague_outbreak_location.GetName] is not so far away.
The Plague Approaches

Crowds of strangers are pouring into [bordering_province.GetName]. Most are common folk fleeing the plague that has reached [infected_province.GetName], just beyond our borders. Some have lost their whole families, some are trying to save theirs, and a few are pedlars and merchants who had an easier time of the road. All of them have seen horrors, and few will speak of it. Those who do warn everyone to bar their doors, or pack and run.
We must survive this.
Hospices will be needed.
Heretics are bringing the plague here!
Let the plague come.
When will it end?
The Empire Ravaged by Plague

The Great Plague has spread across the Empire, from the Middle Mountains to the Black Mountains. The temples of Sigmar are full of the dying, the Reik carries bloated corpses past Altdorf's empty quays, and the priests of Morr cannot dig the pits fast enough. In the deep forests, they say, the Beastmen grow bold.
Bretonnia Ravaged by Plague

Death walks through Bretonnia. The peasants die in their hovels by the thousand while the knights pray at the grails and find no answer. The Lady seems deaf to her people, and in the marshes of Mousillon, they say, something is glad.
Kislev Ravaged by Plague

The Great Plague has reached the oblasts of Kislev. The stanitsas stand silent on the steppe, their people dead or fled, and the ravens feast. Not even the winter can kill it, and the Ice Witches whisper that the north is watching and waiting.
Tilea Ravaged by Plague

The Great Plague is reaping the city-states of Tilea. The merchant princes have shut themselves in their palazzos, the mercenary companies have scattered to the hills, and in the markets of Miragliano the corpses lie where they fell. Some say the plague rose from the canals, and that there are things moving beneath them.
Estalia Ravaged by Plague

Panic grips Estalia as the Great Plague claims its victims. The faithful crowd the temples of Myrmidia to beg the Lady of Battle for a war they can fight, but this enemy has no face. Ships from Magritta are turned away from every harbour.
The Border Princes Ravaged by Plague

The Great Plague has come to the Border Princes, and in that lawless country there is no one to stop it. Petty lords die in their towers, bandits and refugees alike rot by the roadsides, and the greenskins of the Badlands gather to pick over what is left.
Araby Ravaged by Plague

An ominous shadow lies over the sultanates of Araby as the Great Plague leaves little but grief in its wake. The caravans no longer cross the desert, the bazaars are empty, and the hearts of many are torn, asking why [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] would let this come to pass.
Norsca Ravaged by Plague

Not even the frozen north is safe. The Great Plague has struck the Norscan tribes, and their longhouses stand empty under the snow. The shamans of the Plague God sing over the dead, and the other tribes burn whole villages to keep the rot away.
The Dwarf Holds Ravaged by Plague

Even the Dwarfs, hardiest of all the peoples, are dying. The Great Plague has found its way into the deep halls of the Karaz Ankor, and the Book of Grudges is filling with a name no Dwarf can strike: the sickness itself, and the Skaven who some say brought it from below.
Albion Ravaged by Plague

The Great Plague has crossed the sea to mist-shrouded Albion. The tribes die in their hill-forts and the Truthsayers can do nothing, and the fog over the island now carries the stench of the pyres to every passing ship.
Ulthuan Ravaged by Plague

The unthinkable has happened: the Great Plague has reached Ulthuan. The shining cities of the Asur are hung with the white of mourning, and in the temples of Isha the priestesses weep without end. The elves have not known such death since the Sundering.
Lustria Ravaged by Plague

The jungles of Lustria are rotting. The Great Plague runs wild in the heat, and the corpses of men and beasts swell in the steaming undergrowth. The Lizardmen's priests read in it the work of the Ruinous Powers, and the Slann are said to be stirring in their temple-cities.

column2: the Lustrian Fever
Alas!
You can no longer ignore the irritation in your throat, you begin to violently cough.
One moment you are shivering, the next you are sweating, and overall you feel awful.
A sudden gurgling and feeling of pressure in your gut is all the warning you have before you are forced to make a dash for the privy.
A queasy feeling overcomes you and you feel an immediate urge to vomit.
A dull pain begins to throb behind your eyes.
A sudden shooting pain strikes your chest. After a moment of agony it passes... for now.
You double over in pain as you are suddenly beset by painful cramps.
Alerted by a growing feeling of itchiness, you are appalled to notice the appearance of a bright red rash on your body.
Sharp pains in your abdomen cause you to clutch at your stomach.
As the day drags on, seemingly never ending, you can barely keep your eyes open. You seem to have no energy at all.
Although you can't quite put your finger on what's wrong, you don't feel quite right.
Your swollen lymphs have blackened and burst, spewing out blood and pus. You have contracted the Black Plague.
What started out as a mere cough has now turned into shaking chills, shortness of breath and stabs of severe pain in the chest. You have contracted the Rattlelung.
Repulsive sores and abscesses are spreading across your body, originating from the groin. You have contracted the Kruts.
You are suffering of a heavy cough with bloody phlegm. Food has lost its appeal and no amount of sleep seems to remedy your fatigue. You have contracted the Weevil Cough.
You feel as if you are burning up and at times you have difficulties distinguishing between dreams and reality. You have contracted the Ochre Pox.
Yesterday lesions appeared on your face and swiftly spread across your body. Now they have turned to shriveled white patches of skin. You have contracted the Ghoulpox.
You are suffering a high fever and green boils have slowly spread across your entire body. You have contracted the Green Pox.
You are confined to your bed, your body racked with aches and chills. You have contracted the Flu.
You spend most of your waking hours on the privy, where you frequently pass a loose, bloody stool. You have contracted the Bloody Flux.
You are pained with hot, swollen joints which disturb your sleep. You have contracted Gout.
When you are not passing a loose stool in the chamber pot, you are bent over it, retching. You are suffering from Food Poisoning.
You feel possessed, full of uncontrollable excitement and irrational fears! You have contracted Rabies.
The symptoms which have troubled you lately were a sign of something much worse. You have Cancer.

A fever has burned in you since the jungle, and red welts creep across your skin. Your head pounds and your limbs feel full of lead. It is the Lustrian Fever, and the physicians of the Old World have no remedy for it.
Your mind is clouded and a dull red rash is spreading across your body. You feel hot and your joints ache. You have contracted the Red Pox.

I can no longer bear the revulsion of the faces of the people I meet. Although most try to hide their reaction, I have grown to recognize even the slightest flinch when their gaze tracks over my face.\nNo more! I will accept that I am disfigured and don a mask.
Being at sea for a long time has made me feel ill. And it is not a matter of being seasick mind you. I feel very tired, have constant pain in my legs and whenever I wake up, my joints ache all over.
Maybe we should head back to port...

After being examined by my physician [From.GetFirstName], [From.GetSheHe] told me to take it easy during the coming weeks. I am also instructed to eat a special diet consisting mostly of fruit and vegetables in order to cure my Scurvy.
If you say so.
After eating plenty of different fruit and vegetables, I finally feel well. The pain is gone and I am in a much better state! I am sure to avoid scurvy if I eat an orange.
Er... door hinge?

My [GetFromRelation], [From.GetTitledFirstName], has not been [From.GetHerselfHimself] lately. I have noticed how [From.GetSheHe] has lost weight and been overcome by episodes of intense fatigue. Apparently the underlying cause is cancerous growth which is sucking the life out of [From.GetHerHim].

During the last few days my [GetFromRelation], [From.GetTitledFirstName], has been clutching at [From.GetHerHis] stomach and made frequent visits to the privy. I have now been informed that [From.GetSheHe] is suffering from the Bloody Flux.
Recently I have noticed the pitiful state of my [GetFromRelation], [From.GetTitledFirstName]. I have just been informed that the cause of [From.GetHerHis] aches and fatigue is a case of the flu.
During the last few days my [GetFromRelation], [From.GetTitledFirstName], has not been able to keep any drink or food down. It seems as if [From.GetSheHe] is suffering from food poisoning.

For some time now, my [GetFromRelation], [From.GetTitledFirstName], has been complaining about [From.GetHerHis] painful joints. Apparently they frequently swell up, becoming hot and aching for several hours.

These are dark days. My [GetFromRelation], [From.GetTitledFirstName], has been burning with fever and covered in red welts ever since the jungle. I have just been told that it is the Lustrian Fever, for which the Old World knows no cure.

These are dark days. My [GetFromRelation], [From.GetTitledFirstName], has been beset by strange boils and a high fever. I have just been informed that [From.GetHerHis] affliction is indeed the Green Pox.

These are dark days. When my [GetFromRelation], [From.GetTitledFirstName], was beset by a high fever and could not stop vomiting, we feared the worst. The suspicions are now confirmed. [From.GetHerHisCap] affliction is indeed the dreaded Black Plague.

For some time now my [GetFromRelation], [From.GetTitledFirstName], has been overcome with fatigue and troubled by a persistent cough. I have now been informed that the symptoms are due to the Rattlelung.

During the last few days, my [GetFromRelation] [From.GetTitledFirstName], has been acting strangely indeed! I have just been informed that [From.GetHerHis] aggressive behaviour and episodes of extreme anxiety have been caused by rabies.
These are dark days. My [GetFromRelation], [From.GetTitledFirstName], has been beset by oozing lesions and a high fever. I have just been informed that [From.GetHerHis] affliction is indeed Ghoulpox.

My [GetFromRelation], [From.GetTitledFirstName], has not been quite [From.GetHerselfHimself] lately. For a while now, I have noticed [From.GetHerHim] looking tired and thin. I have just been informed of the cause - [From.GetFirstName] has contracted the Kruts!

These are dark days. My [GetFromRelation], [From.GetTitledFirstName], has been growing weaker and weaker over the last few weeks and I have just been informed that [From.GetHerHis] affliction is indeed the Weevil Cough.

These are dark days. My [GetFromRelation], [From.GetTitledFirstName], has been beset by a high fever for several days and I have just been informed that [From.GetHerHis] affliction is indeed the Ochre Pox.

These are dark days. My [GetFromRelation], [From.GetTitledFirstName], has been beset by strange rashes and episodes of delirium over the last few weeks. I have just been informed that [From.GetHerHis] affliction is indeed the Red Pox.
Call for my Court Physician at once!
Sickness and death awaits us all. Stop pestering me.
I must find a court physician!
You there – tend to my [GetFromRelation] immediately!

For some time now, my [GetFromRelation] [From.GetTitledFirstName] has been avoiding me. [From.GetSheHeCap] has not visited my bedchamber for several weeks. When I have demanded to know why [From.GetSheHe] has given me nothing but feeble excuses. Today I overheard a couple of [From.GetHerHis] servants gossiping. They said [From.GetFirstName] has caught the Kruts!
So [From.GetSheHe] is the one who brought this upon me! What a [GetRootFromInsult]!
I will show that [GetRootFromInsult] what I do with traitors!
Imprison §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! and §Y[syphilis_lover.GetTitledFirstName]§!, whom your spies believe is [From.GetHerHis] lover.\n
Imprison §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§!.\n
[Root.Religion.GetHighGodName], am I to blame? I will not give up until [From.GetSheHe] is well again!
The poor thing! I will do what I can for [From.GetHerHim].
Take care of §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§!, attempting to nurse [From.GetHerHim] back to health.\n
You shouldn't believe everything you hear. Surely there's another reason.
After what seems like forever, the wound from your maiming has healed. The scar will stay.
The wound from your maiming is stinking and oozing pus. The pain is unbearable and the courtiers avoid you like death itself.
Finally
That's not good.
Your Infection has put you in grave danger on multiple occasions. The pain and foul smell have finally subsided and your wound looks clean.
I feel better.
You realize you have been free from your Cough for a few days now. Being able to sleep at night without waking up coughing is a blessing.
Your Fever has passed and you regain some strength and focus in your daily routine.
After a very troublesome period, your Diarrhea has finally stopped.
Your Vomiting has finally stopped and you can start eating regular meals again.
The Chest Pains you have been experiencing lately seem to have stopped. The Pains have been occurring less frequently, until recently they just disappeared.
You haven't had any severe Cramps for some time now, whatever caused them must have been dealt with.
Whatever was left of your Rash is no longer visible, and the spot where it was is no longer itching or causing pain.
Your pressing Headache has gone away, and you can focus your mind on things again.
Excruciating Abdominal Pains have been disabling you lately, but now that you come to think of it, they are no longer there.
The sense of Fatigue that has been present lately now seems to have disappeared, and you once again have the energy to carry out your duties.
Your Malaise is no more. If it wasn't just imagination then whatever caused it must have disappeared.
You have recovered well from the Flu, now the coughing, fever, and headache are just unpleasant memories.
After some very worrying dehydration and abdominal pains, your Bloody Flux has finally ended.
Excruciating pain and stiff joints have been tormenting you, but they are now much less severe. Gout is no longer a problem.
Your violent vomiting and diarrhea have gone away, you have recovered from what must have been Food Poisoning.
The violent outbursts coupled with losses of consciousness, which seemed like a nightmare, is now just a memory. You have survived Rabies.
Your tumors are no more, and it seems the disease is no longer spreading. It will be a while until you are completely back to normal but the Cancer is gone.
Your cough has subsided and the ill-boding fever has left your body. You have survived the Rattlelung.
The sores on your body have vanished and you are almost back to your regular self. You are rid of the Kruts.
You awake rejuvenated. After some moments of disbelief you realize that your cough has passed and your appetite has returned. You have survived the Weevil Cough.
Your delirium has lifted and your temperature is back to normal. You have beaten the Ochre Pox.
A vigor has returned to you as the aches from your recent disease leaves your body. You have survived the Red Pox.
You're not sure how it happened, but your skin has returned to a healthy color and the abscesses are gone. It would seem you have survived the Black Plague.
The feverish state you've been stuck in lately is replaced by a new energy. Meanwhile the green boils are gone.
The many shrivelled patches on your body have faded, almost all of them gone now. So much for the Ghoulpox.
The fever that has burned in you since the jungle has broken at last and the welts are fading. You have survived the Lustrian Fever, which is more than most colonists can say.

Your Court Physician [From.GetBestName] has come to see you and offers treatment for your illness. [From.GetSheHeCap] explains that there are several different types of treatment [From.GetSheHe] can offer.
My life is in your hands.
§Y[From.GetBestName]§! will perform an experimental treatment. The outcome of this treatment can be extreme. The risk of this treatment will vary depending on [From.GetHerHis] capabilities.
As long as you know what you're doing.

§Y[From.GetBestName]§! will perform some well tested treatment. There is a chance that the treatment has negative effects. The risk of this treatment will vary depending on [From.GetHerHis] capabilities.
Please do only what is necessary.

§Y[From.GetBestName]§! will make you more comfortable in your current state. This treatment will have a very small chance of going badly, but the positive effects will not have much impact. The risk of this treatment will vary depending on [From.GetHerHis] capabilities.
These treatments sound scary.
You prefer to be left to your own devices.\n
I trust your knowledge, oh wise one.
§Y[From.GetBestName]§! will perform a mystical treatment. The outcome of this treatment is uncertain. The risk of this treatment will vary depending on [From.GetHerHis] capabilities.
Come on, [From.GetFirstName], let's try something new. I insist.
§Y[From.GetBestName]§! will perform an experimental treatment. The outcome of this treatment can be extreme. The risk of this treatment will vary depending on [From.GetHerHis] capabilities.

The pot which [FromFrom.GetBestName] brought with [FromFrom.GetHerHim] to your chambers emitted a strange buzzing sound. Before you could stop [FromFrom.GetHerHim] [FromFrom.GetSheHe] threw it on the floor, where it exploded in a cloud of pottery shards and swarm of furious bees. As your physician fled the room, you remained their only target.

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] made you drink a draught of poppy before strapping you down on [FromFrom.GetHerHis] operating table. You almost dozed off while [FromFrom.GetSheHe] prepared [FromFrom.GetHerHis] instruments, but when [FromFrom.GetSheHe] raised a scalpel towards your eye, you felt wide awake. "I am sorry, my [Root.GetLordLady], but we must remove the root of the problem."

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] gave you a draught which tasted most peculiar. It made you feel numb and your eyelids started drooping. "I apologize, my [Root.GetLordLady], but you do not want to be awake for this next part" [FromFrom.GetSheHe] said. Panic hit you and you tried to get up from the operating table, but your limbs would not obey.

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]'s assistant assured [FromFrom.GetHerHim] you were asleep. However, [FromFrom.GetFirstName]'s potion had failed to fully take effect– even though you could neither speak nor move, you were still aware of everything they did to you. You tried to scream and thrash, but you were a prisoner in your own body. The procedure seemed to last forever...

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] informed you that [FromFrom.GetSheHe] had identified the tainted tissue which was the root of your disease, and that removing it would most likely cure you. You were most pleased and agreed to the surgery. However, in hindsight, you wish that [FromFrom.GetFirstName] told you that "the tissue" was your face...

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] buckled the last strap, securing you on the operating table. "I will not lie to you, my [Root.GetLordLady]. This will be excruciatingly painful, but it must be done." You tried to protest when [FromFrom.GetFirstName] brought out the saw, but due to the calming potion [FromFrom.GetSheHe] had made you drink, you slurred the words beyond comprehension.

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] buckled the last strap, securing you on the operating table. "I will not lie to you, my [Root.GetLordLady]. This will be excruciatingly painful, but it must be done." You tried to protest when [FromFrom.GetFirstName] brought out the saw, but due to the calming potion [FromFrom.GetSheHe] had made you drink, you slurred the words beyond comprehension.

You could not believe your eyes when [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] pulled a severed hand from [FromFrom.GetHerHis] satchel. The black spots on its finger sent chills down your spine and you demanded to know where [FromFrom.GetSheHe] got it from. [FromFrom.GetSheHeCap] only hushed you and proceeded to rub the severed hand against your chest.

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] presented you with a potion of the most peculiar sorts. It had neither odor nor taste and possessed the appearance of liquid silver. The metallic potion was easy enough to ingest and you could not understand why this was the risky treatment option.

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] insisted that the only cure for your condition was a naked midnight run. During the next full moon [FromFrom.GetSheHe] forced you to undress and sprint through the wilderness. "Do not stop until your legs give out under you!" [FromFrom.GetSheHe] yelled after you. "Expel the evil through your sweat!"

The powder was yellow and had a delicious scent. You were distraught to see [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] mix it with brimstone and sprinkle it over the still tepid gall-bladder of a beaver. The animal had been found rabid, frothing from the mouth, exhibiting clear signs of the illness. "We fight evil with evil, [Root.GetMasterMistress]."

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] approached you with a small knife. [FromFrom.GetSheHeCap] held your arm steady and made a precise incision, barely breaking your skin. [FromFrom.GetSheHeCap] then proceeded to press something against the wound. It looked like diseased tissue and you shuddered.

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] handed you a plate with a gray powdery substance on it. Apparently it consisted of ground-up scabs from a person in a worse state than you. [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] showed no indication of joking as [FromFrom.GetSheHe] told you to lean in and inhale as much as you could though your nose.
I feel amazing!
I should never have trusted [FromFrom.GetFirstName].
The treatment was successful, but I paid a heavy price...
Curses! May [Root.Religion.GetRandomEvilGodName] strike [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] down!

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] insisted that your humors were out of balance and that the best way to restore them would be through bloodletting. After consulting the astronomical charts, [FromFrom.GetSheHe] decided that you should be bled from your armpits and temples.

The red powder was tantalizing in color. A servant had made the mistake of tasting it in its pure form - his tongue had swollen up badly and [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] had chastized him firmly for it. [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] poured the spice into a chalice of water and stirred it meticulously, before feeding you a spoonful.

Your eyes widened when [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] led a goat into your chambers. The foul smell of its flatulence made you both cover your noses, but the physician pulled your hand away. "Apologies, my [Root.GetLordLady], this is the treatment." [FromFrom.GetSheHeCap] recommended deep breaths.

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] brought you a concoction made from buckthorn and senna. At first you thought the potion ineffectual, but later the same day you felt a churning in your bowels which sent you running for the privy. As you howled in anguish, [FromFrom.GetFirstName] assured you that the foulness was expelled with your feces.

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] told you to undress and then kneel with your buttocks raised. That was awkward enough, but when you saw the instrument in [FromFrom.GetHerHis] hands you almost bolted. [FromFrom.GetFirstName] must have noticed, because [FromFrom.GetSheHe] patted you calmingly on the shoulder and told you to stop clenching.

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] entered your chambers with an earthenware jar cradled in [FromFrom.GetHerHis] arms and came to sit by your bed. [FromFrom.GetSheHeCap] pulled a leech from the jar and gave it a most tender look before carefully placing it on your face. "Remain still, my [Root.GetLordLady]. Better not disturb their feeding."

When [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] entered your chambers [FromFrom.GetSheHe] was followed by an air most foul. The stench seemed to originate from the jar in [FromFrom.GetHerHis] hands– "a mixture of cow's dung and herbs for your poultice, [Root.GetMasterMistress]". When [FromFrom.GetFirstName] proceeded to smear it on your chest you almost retched.

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] presented you with the charred carcass of a cat and prompted you to dig in. As you ate, [FromFrom.GetSheHe] told you how [FromFrom.GetSheHe] had chased the plump feline around your holdings for hours. You felt as if [FromFrom.GetSheHe] wanted praise for [FromFrom.GetHerHis] hard work, but the vile taste of the meal kept you silent.

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] brought a croaking bucket to your chambers and told you to expose your upper body. [FromFrom.GetSheHeCap] grabbed a toad, gutted it with a deft hand and proceeded to place the still twitching carcass on your chest. [FromFrom.GetFirstName] continued until the bucket was empty and your torso was covered.

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] came to your chambers and offered you a draught which was yellow in color. [FromFrom.GetSheHeCap] told you to pinch your nose as you drank it. When the tepid liquid passed your lips you almost immediately spat it out again. You demanded to know the content and [FromFrom.GetSheHe] revealed that it was fresh urine from a pregnant sow.

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] lowered [FromFrom.GetHerHis] hand into the bucket [FromFrom.GetSheHe] brought to to your chambers. When [FromFrom.GetSheHe] pulled it out again a little fish was wriggling between [FromFrom.GetHerHis] fingers. "Open wide" [FromFrom.GetSheHe] prompted you and dropped it in your mouth. You struggled not to retch as it tickled the back of your throat.
I actually feel better.
I probably shouldn't have agreed to this...

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] was convinced that the best course of treatment would be some rest. [FromFrom.GetSheHeCap] surrounded you in soft pillows and gently tucked you in under many layers of blankets. Before [FromFrom.GetFirstName] left your chambers, [FromFrom.GetSheHe] pulled your curtains shut. It was noon.

The steam rose from the cup as [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] stirred the green powder in it. [FromFrom.GetSheHeCap] explained the healing properties of the herb at length, before motioning for you to drink it. "The root is in there, too", [FromFrom.GetSheHe] boastfully revealed.

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] contributed your ailments to an unsound diet. To revitalize your body [FromFrom.GetSheHe] insisted you consume only raw vegetables and herbal teas for a fortnight. So as not to tempt you, [FromFrom.GetSheHe] confiscated your stash of treats. [FromFrom.GetSheHeCap] never returned them.

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] told you to lie down on your bed and then to offer [FromFrom.GetHerHim] your hands. Firmly [FromFrom.GetSheHe] rubbed and slapped your palms until they were red, and then repeated the treatment on your soles. As a finishing touch [FromFrom.GetSheHe] pinched you gently up and down your limbs.

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] offered you a clear potion in a gilded vial. As you had tasted some previous remedies of [FromFrom.GetFirstName]'s you were worried at first, but as you drank it you could detect neither odor nor taste. You inquired about the ingredients, but [FromFrom.GetSheHe] told you that it was a secret recipe.

Relax your breathing, [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] instructed you. The feather in [FromFrom.GetHerHis] hand looked almost ethereal as [FromFrom.GetSheHe] began to gently brush you under your nose. "Evil, begone!" [FromFrom.GetSheHe] urged, as the sneezing began.

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] arranged a small ceremony in your name. Once your family and closest entourage were all gathered in the main hall, the [From.Religion.GetPriestTitle] gave a sermon highlighting your virtue and benevolence. Their united prayers will surely speed your recovery.

You spent many evenings with [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName], as [FromFrom.GetSheHe] recited you stories from [Root.Religion.GetScriptureName], until you were fast asleep. The routine has been comforting.

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] called on the [From.Religion.GetPriestTitle] to bring forth the finest singer in the court, which turned out to be a young child with a bright tenor voice. For several days in a row, the child sang you to sleep. How soothing.

The water was steaming hot when [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] let the honey drip into it. It dissolved almost instantly, but [FromFrom.GetSheHe] stirred it for a long time. "That's it?", you finally asked. [FromFrom.GetSheHeCap] nodded, and you drank the tea.
I feel better, I think.
Maybe I should have insisted on some other treatment...

[From.GetTitledName] states that [From.GetHerHis] extensive medical experience leads [From.GetHerHim] to the certain conclusion that your symptoms point to Cancer. [From.GetSheHeCap] insists that you follow [From.GetHerHis] instructions.

[From.GetTitledName] thinks your symptoms may point to Canter. [From.GetSheHeCap] expresses confusion as to why this would be a problem, but insists that you follow [From.GetHerHis] instructions anyway.
[From.GetTitledName] thinks your symptoms point to Cancer. [From.GetSheHeCap] insists that you follow [From.GetHerHis] instructions.
[From.GetTitledName] hesitantly suggests that your symptoms may point to Cancer. [From.GetSheHeCap] insists that you follow [From.GetHerHis] instructions.
